heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings and their chaining values cv = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: within one chaining value the 2^26 table values F(a0) behave as independent uniform words (expected occupancy occ = 1 - (1 - 2^-26)^(2^26), uniform tags, 160 occ 2^26 / 2^32 claws per scan word); F7 has probability |F7|/2^32; the X_j and the online works W_j of different chaining values are independent (proof.md Lemma 3, Section 7).
heuristics.scope: The expected claw count, the mean online work wbar (hence V_MAX), the independence used by Bernstein's inequality for the cap (Lemma 3) and the product over chaining values in the success bound (proof.md Sections 5, 7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our C port at n0 = 2^26 measured occupancy 0.63216 and claws/expected 0.99898 over 2^20 scan words; the organizer experiment p1-online-r38 reports occupancy, claws and expected claws on seed-drawn chaining values. The scan words u0 + n are distinct and u0 is a fresh random word per chaining value, so the scan adds no dependence (proof.md Section 3).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem: within each chaining value the table values F(a0), their tags and the claws found are taken to follow the per-chaining-value random-function law; independent first blocks do not by themselves prove it. Checked at reduced and full table size on a few chaining values, not on 2^57.7 of them.

heuristics.statement: For the claws the procedure finds, Pr[C1 and C2 and G and F7] = q_pf = 57,726,359,870,197 x 287,309,824 / 2^90 = 2^-16.1877, the rate enumerated exhaustively over all 2^32 words (P(C1) = 1/8, |C1 and C2| = 53,096,854, the window-R = 9 G count 57,726,359,870,197, |F7| = 287,309,824); the stage rates 1/8, 2^-6.3379, 2^-12.2857 set the mean post-filter cost.
heuristics.scope: The good pairs per chaining value (5,683.36) and the mean post-filter work in wbar (proof.md Sections 5, 6).
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact rationals for uniform words; the claws' a1 = u - h(a0, cv) and their a0 are the visible table entries (last write wins). Development support: C-port stage rates C1 0.12501, C2|C1 2^-3.3379, G 2^-5.996 on real claws, a 36-chaining-value panel (claw/base 0.991 to 1.124) and 294 good pairs. The counted chain equals the definitions on the real words (0 mismatches; selftest, p1-online-r38).
heuristics.limitations: A premise that the exhaustive rates hold for the claws found; F7 is chaining-value dependent (measured heterogeneity 1.254).

heuristics.statement: A good pair is accepted by step 3b with probability q3r >= q3_model x 2^32 / 160 = 2^-71.1710, where q3_model = 2^-95.8491 is the accepted-event good-pair acceptance rate before row 16 (row 16 has probability 160/2^32 and a P1 good pair has passed it). q3_model is stated and derived in proof.md Section 9 so it is auditable from the package alone.
heuristics.extrapolation: The acceptance predicate of step 3b reads only W8, W9, W16..W37 (W10..W15 are S's fixed words; W16..W37 are fixed by W0..W15). A P1 good pair (a0, a1 free) and a row-16-passing A0-variant (A_{-1} uniform) both present (W8, W9) uniform over the same row-16-passing set, so the predicate is the same function of same-law inputs and R = 1 by construction (proof.md Section 9). The development ratio estimate (1.0162, 512 SMC prefixes, not preregistered) is consistent context, not the basis.
heuristics.limitations: A declared premise: q3_model is a one-sided 99% lower bound from preregistered Monte-Carlo estimates whose construction is given in proof.md Section 9; the complete event (about 2^-71 per good pair) is not observed by any organizer run. A ratio R < 1 would raise the time by at most log2(1/R) bit.

heuristics.statement: For a uniform chaining value let J be the number of good pairs accepted by step 3b over all 2^32 scan words. E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J]: given one accepted pair, a chaining value has on average at most 2^-7.5 others.
heuristics.scope: The Bonferroni factor (1 - 2^-8.5) per chaining value. Lemma 4 (proof.md Section 7) derives E[X_j(X_j-1)]/E[X_j] <= E[J(J-1)]/E[J] exactly from the distinct scan words u0 + n with u0 uniform; no premise on the scan is used.
heuristics.extrapolation: E[J] = 2^-54.70; under independence given cv, E[J(J-1)]/E[J] would be about 2^-54.70, so the premise allows positive dependence or heterogeneity up to 2^47.2 above it: it fails only if, given one accepted pair, each of the other ~2^16.47 good pairs of that chaining value is accepted with probability above 2^-23.97 on average instead of 2^-71.2. Support: the claws of one chaining value are distinct pairs with distinct (W0, W1) (distinct_pairs in both organizer experiments); acceptance is a function of the pair's W0..W9, of which W8, W9 read (a0, a1) only; F7, the one post-filter reading cv, has measured heterogeneity 1.254 over 36 chaining values.
heuristics.limitations: A declared premise: the complete event (about 2^-71 per good pair) cannot be sampled and no experiment tests the bound; it rests on the derivation, its 2^47 slack and the measured stages, not on observed accepted pairs.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^78 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^78 is the largest allowance; it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (78.09276).
heuristics.extrapolation: A_C = 2^78 is the exact characteristic-search allowance accepted in our accepted entry fb176310 (sha256-r38, 95.90375); we adopt that accepted charge rather than a re-run or an external log.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement: its support is that fb176310 was accepted at this same allowance; we did not rerun the search. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 84.96819.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) is obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^74 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^74).
heuristics.extrapolation: A_S = 2^74 is the exact Step-1-solve allowance accepted in our accepted entry fb176310; selftest checks that the transcribed pair S reproduces and passes every test of rows 16..21 with equal outputs. We adopt the accepted charge, not an external log.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement: fb176310 was accepted at this same allowance. The preprocessing peak memory (2^28.094) that sets the claimed peak (H6) is a separately charged upper bound.

heuristics.statement: All development computation of this package, whether or not the procedure reads its output (exhaustive passes, C ports, the q3 and ratio studies, the F7 measurement, checks, failed runs and reruns), is at most DEV = 2^70 target compressions, and DEV is charged in full in the time.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^70 x C operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: Hardware envelope (the bound for this allowance): every code execution of the project (10-05 to 10-20) ran on a 24-thread workstation with one GPU, a 12-thread server and one 32-vCPU cloud machine: at most 68 threads and one GPU for 1.3824 x 10^6 s at 2^40 word operations per thread-second and 2^47 per GPU-second, below 2^68.1 operations = 2^56.7 compressions, under DEV by more than 2^13.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement: the hardware envelope above is the bound; it rests on the project's machine list and dates, and is more than 2^13 below the charge.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 (256-bit word RAM) the claw table's 4-byte slots are packed eight to a 256-bit word: a table load is 7 operations and a store (read-modify-write) 11; the per-chaining-value reset of the table to SENT is 2^23 word stores of 5 operations (store 1, address add 1, loop 3). Every other operation of the procedure, including each work-counter add (1), the empty-slot test (2) and step 3b, is counted at the unit costs of fb176310 (S0/S1/s0/s1 8, CH 3, MAJ 4, compare-and-branch 2, the rest 1).
heuristics.scope: The counted operations of the online procedure (proof.md Sections 4, 5): 437.064 per claw (scan, post-filters, reset and build) and 3,014 per step 3b.
heuristics.extrapolation: run_claw counts every operation; selftest checks the counted run against the per-u charge of Section 5; our C port's scan count 425.592 per u (before packed access and counters) matches the straight-line count.
heuristics.limitations: The ledger is an exact analytic count read from the code, not a measurement; it does not rely on the organizer runs' counted_ops (reduced size). The unit costs are the fb176310 convention; the packed access sequence is the explicit list of proof.md Section 4.

heuristics.statement: The peak memory is the maximum over the counted phases, <= 2^28.094 bytes: online, the table 2^28 bytes plus advice (912 bytes), registers, scan state and the program code and implementation storage (a few KiB, included per the cost model), below 2^28 + 2^14; the preprocessing peak, the Step-1 solve of P8, measured by its author at 279,720 KB = 2^28.094 bytes.
heuristics.scope: The memory metric and the score 83.95932 + (28.094 - 20) = 92.05332.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our C port of the claw at n0 = 2^26 ran with a peak resident set of 264,224 KiB = 2^28.011 bytes (/usr/bin/time -v); the organizer experiments run the procedure at 2^16 slots within the sandbox.
heuristics.limitations: The 2^28.094 figure is a charged upper bound taken from its author's report, not our measurement.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; step 3b accepts a pair only if A34..A37, E34..E37 of both members are equal, so every output is a collision (Lemma 1, proof.md Section 1).

Algorithm (proof.md Sections 2, 3; experiments/p1claw38.py): per chaining value a 2^26-slot table over a0 in window R = 9 (4-byte slots packed in 256-bit words, last write wins) and a scan of the 2^28 distinct words u = u0 + n; a claw (a0, u) has E16x = F(a0) + s0(u) - u in the 160-word row-16 set; claws pass the post-filters C1, C2, G, F7 on the real words; every good pair runs step 3b (Step 2, rows 16..37 of both members, the P8 tests of rows 16..21 with early abort, output comparison).

Cost: N_CV = 231,845,170,969,091,846 chaining values; online work counted per operation (packed load 7, store 11, work-counter adds, step 3b 3,014) with mean wbar = 1.854236e11 per chaining value (table reset 2^23 x 5 included), capped at V_MAX = ceil((1 + 2^-16) N_CV wbar), cap tested per chaining value, OVER = vmax = 67,093,940,669,171. N = (2^78 + 2^74 + 2^70) C + N_FB (C + 35) + V_MAX + OVER + FIN = 51,300,194,368,156,548,298,038,655,828 = 2^83.95932 compressions (C = 2,728).

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1 (independent uniform chaining values), H1-P1 (q_pf = 2^-16.1877 for claws), H2-P1 (q3r >= 2^-71.1710 per good pair) and H3-P1 (E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J]); Lemma 4 reduces the within-chaining-value term to H3-P1 exactly; Bonferroni per chaining value, independence across them, and Bernstein's inequality for the cap (Lemma 3, halt probability < 2^-107,000).

Memory: peak 2^28.094 bytes = maximum over the counted phases: online, the 2^28-byte table plus advice, registers and state (below 2^28 + 2^14); the Step-1 solve of P8, measured by its author at 279,720 KB. H6. Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 83.95932 + 8.094 = 92.05332. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.
